option_a_dns_resolution_failure.symptom: API returns connection errors (ENOTFOUND / getaddrinfo failed) while database container is running and healthy
option_a_dns_resolution_failure.root_cause: DNS resolution failure or corrupted /etc/hosts entry resolving postgres hostname to wrong IP (127.0.0.1) or failing lookup before TCP handshake even begins.
option_a_dns_resolution_failure.diagnostic_proof: Testing direct IP connectivity succeeds while hostname lookup fails (`nslookup`/`getent hosts`), proving the database is healthy and the fault lies strictly in DNS/name resolution.

option_b_slow_dependency.symptom: GET /live returns 200 OK, yet real API latency jumps from 200ms to 5000ms and requests time out
option_b_slow_dependency.root_cause: Grey failure (slow database/downstream dependency without strict query/socket timeouts). Because /live only checks Node event-loop health, it stays green while database-dependent routes hold open pool connections until saturation.
option_b_slow_dependency.diagnostic_proof: Correlating http_request_duration_seconds p95 spike against DB query timings and http_requests_in_flight gauge reveals connection pool saturation caused by slow downstream responses.

option_c_partial_read_only_failure.symptom: GET endpoints work normally and aggregate 'up' monitoring stays green, while all POST/PUT/DELETE mutations fail
option_c_partial_read_only_failure.root_cause: Partial failure caused by database failover to a read-only replica (`default_transaction_read_only=on`), disk-full read-only filesystem remount, or split-brain write-leader loss. Aggregate health checks executing only `SELECT 1` miss write-path failure completely.
option_c_partial_read_only_failure.diagnostic_proof: Checking `SHOW transaction_read_only;` on PostgreSQL and slicing `http_requests_total` by `method` immediately isolates 100% failure on POST/PUT/DELETE with 0% failure on GET.
